name: Sorrento Sailing Couta Boat Club
signature: Australia's largest couta boat fleet — a uniquely Peninsula sailing tradition with racing, learn-to-sail, and panoramic bay views from the clubhouse
editorNote:
The Sorrento Sailing Couta Boat Club is one of the most distinctive sailing clubs in Australia — home to the country's largest fleet of couta boats, the traditional gaff-rigged wooden vessels that were once the workhorses of Port Phillip Bay's commercial fishing fleet and are now the Peninsula's most iconic sailing sight.

Weekend couta boat racing from the Sorrento foreshore is a summer spectacle worth timing a visit around — a fleet of wooden boats with distinctive brown sails tacking across the bay against the Portsea backdrop. The club runs learn-to-sail programs for all ages from 5 years upward, and the clubhouse has panoramic bay views that rival any restaurant on the foreshore.

Open to visitors and new members. The junior sailing program is one of the strongest on the Peninsula.
whyWeGo: Couta boat racing on the bay — the most distinctively Peninsula sailing experience in the country.
ifOnlyOneThing: Be on the Sorrento foreshore on a Saturday morning when the couta boat fleet starts racing. Brown sails, wooden hulls, Bay backdrop — it is unlike anything else.
